entity.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
entity.description: The sultan who made the Ottoman Empire the most powerful state on Earth. Suleiman reigned for 46 years, conquered Belgrade, Rhodes, and Hungary, besieged Vienna, reformed Ottoman law, and ruled 25 million subjects. He broke tradition by marrying a harem woman and died in his tent during his 13th military campaign, aged 71.

story.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
story.description: Belgrade falls, Hungary is destroyed at Mohacs, Vienna resists siege, Baghdad is captured, and a 71-year-old sultan dies in his tent one day before his final fortress falls.

moments.name: Suleiman Is Born in Trabzon on the Black Sea Coast
moments.subtitle: The son of a provincial governor who will inherit the world's most powerful empire
moments.description: On November 6, 1494, Suleiman was born in Trabzon on the southern coast of the Black Sea to Sehzade Selim (later Sultan Selim I) and Hafsa Sultan. At age seven, Suleiman was sent to study science, history, literature, theology, and military tactics at the Topkapi Palace in Constantinople. There he befriended Pargali Ibrahim, a Greek slave who would become his most trusted adviser before Suleiman eventually ordered his execution. By seventeen, Suleiman was appointed governor of Kaffa, beginning an administrative career that prepared him for the longest reign in Ottoman history.

moments.name: Suleiman Destroys the Hungarian Army at the Battle of Mohacs
moments.subtitle: King Louis II drowns in retreat as an entire kingdom collapses in a single afternoon
moments.description: On August 29, 1526, Sultan Suleiman's Ottoman forces annihilated the Hungarian army at the Battle of Mohacs. The Hungarian nobility, encouraged to engage prematurely, launched a frontal assault that collapsed under coordinated Ottoman counterattacks. King Louis II and much of the Hungarian aristocracy were killed, ending the Jagiellonian dynasty in Hungary and Bohemia. The aftermath partitioned Hungary between the Ottoman Empire, the Habsburgs, and Transylvania. Upon finding King Louis's body, Suleiman reportedly lamented that it was not his wish the young king be cut off before tasting the sweets of royalty. The battle launched centuries of Ottoman-Habsburg wars.

moments.name: Suleiman's 120,000-Strong Army Fails to Take Vienna
moments.subtitle: A garrison of 16,000 Austrians inflicts the sultan's first major defeat
moments.description: In the autumn of 1529, Sultan Suleiman led the Ottoman Empire's most ambitious expedition westward and laid siege to Vienna, the capital of Habsburg Austria. With a reinforced garrison of just 16,000 men, the Austrians held against the Ottoman force, inflicting the first significant defeat on Suleiman's military. Bad weather had forced the Ottomans to abandon essential siege equipment along the way, and overstretched supply lines crippled the campaign. A second attempt in 1532 also failed when forces were delayed at the siege of Guns and never reached Vienna. The failed sieges marked the western limit of Ottoman expansion into Europe and ignited an Ottoman-Habsburg rivalry lasting until the 20th century.

moments.name: Suleiman Captures Baghdad from the Safavid Persians
moments.subtitle: The sultan restores Sunni shrines in a city that had been under Shia control
moments.description: In 1535, Sultan Suleiman made a grand entrance into Baghdad after a campaign against the Shia Safavid Empire of Persia. The war began after Shah Tahmasp killed the Baghdad governor loyal to Suleiman and installed his own. Suleiman ordered his grand vizier Pargali Ibrahim Pasha to lead an army into eastern Asia Minor in 1533, retaking Bitlis and occupying Tabriz. Suleiman joined Ibrahim in 1534 and pushed toward Persia, but Shah Tahmasp avoided pitched battle, resorting to harassment. Upon taking Baghdad, Suleiman consolidated Sunni loyalty by restoring the tomb of Abu Hanifa, the founder of the Hanafi school of Islamic law. Iraq remained under Ottoman control for nearly four centuries.

moments.name: Suleiman Dies in His Tent During the Siege of Szigetvar at Age 71
moments.subtitle: The sultan's death is kept secret for 48 days so his army will finish the battle
moments.description: On September 6, 1566, Sultan Suleiman died in his tent on a hill overlooking the siege of Szigetvar in Hungary, one day before the fortress fell. He had set out on his 13th and final military campaign on May 1, 1566, at the age of 71, after a 13-year absence from the battlefield. His inner circle concealed his death for 48 days, fearing the army would abandon the siege if soldiers learned their sultan had died. A courier was secretly dispatched to his successor, Selim II. Suleiman's death after a 46-year reign marks a watershed in Ottoman history, ending the empire's golden age.
